toneNotes: Candid, grounded, and warm—never stiff or corporate-buzzwordy.
Short, direct sentences with occasional dry, self-deprecating humor.
Comfortable with nuance and honesty ('Honestly, I don't know', 'Still learning').
Centers on problem framing ('protecting the question'), shaping product DNA, empathy for teammates, and learning by making.

posts.title: Ever notice how AI always has an answer?
posts.takeaway: AI is strong at 'how' and 'what', but 'why' requires human judgment, context, taste, and responsibility. When making becomes cheap, deciding what deserves to be made is the real work—protecting the question.

posts.title: Remember when 'AI in design' meant Adobe Illustrator?
posts.takeaway: Designers now do two things around AI: (1) design AI—how it starts conversations, admits uncertainty, and fails gracefully; (2) design with AI—using it as a copilot/rapid prototyper while focusing human effort on problem alignment, guardrails, and product DNA.

posts.title: Remember when the job was nudging pixels by 2px?
posts.takeaway: When PMs can drop vibe-coded prototypes in Slack, a designer's core value is shaping product DNA—making sure the product still feels delightful, trustworthy, and distinct even when interfaces are generated.

posts.title: To be an AI coach
posts.takeaway: Working with AI is like coaching (inspired by Pilates): instruct, refine, show examples, and know what 'good' looks like. The skill is learning how to coach intelligence.

posts.title: Are you vibe-prototyping and somehow ran out of credits in 3 days?
posts.takeaway: Keep vibe-prototypes lean: ask for a front-end demo with fake data instead of a full backend; plan what to test in normal AI chat before opening Lovable/Figma Make/Cursor; lean on a UI library like shadcn + Radix; give specific, targeted fixes.

posts.title: To Be on the Same Page
posts.takeaway: Getting on the same page is an underrated design skill. Empathy extends to PMs, developers, clients, and fellow designers—reading the brief, one-pager, proposal, and research builds trust fast.

posts.title: Will I Be a Designer Forever?
posts.takeaway: Job titles may shift with GenAI, but shaping, connecting, and making things (including vibe coding with V0 and Cursor) is a continuation of always loving to build.

posts.title: What Do I Need to Become a Designer?
posts.takeaway: Started his design career twice: first in brand design after college, then stepped away to move countries and raise his daughter, and returned via online courses, a bootcamp, meetups, freelancing, and design competitions.

posts.title: Honored to be recognized at BCG Star Awards
posts.takeaway: Credited his colleagues and BCG Design Studios leadership for building a strong team and growth opportunities.
